solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mother's period home given to daughter, very bright person!

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother, with the possessive S
a term is a period of time, as in a school term
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A family scene: mother's term at home handed over to a clever daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastermind is a person of outstanding intellect, especially one who plans a scheme.

clue.text: Love in the morning associated with us?

parts.note: AM (ante meridiem) marks times in the morning
our is the word for something belonging to or connected with us

explanation.surface: A romantic question: is early-morning love something that belongs to the two of us?
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is the French word for love, used in English for a love affair.

clue.text: Wreck party after hill exercise

indicators.note: after places the party piece behind the hill and exercise pieces

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
PE is physical education, school exercise
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks a party held after a hill-walking exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) is the usual crossword exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo a plan is to wreck or sink it, like a ship hit by a torpedo.

clue.text: Brought up the German wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word for the German is read from bottom to top

parts.note: der is German for the (masculine)

explanation.surface: Someone raised the German wine, as at a table or in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' reverses DER in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a shortened name for red wine, the drink served from the bottle.

clue.text: Ultimately got free rein, mistakenly, to meddle

indicators.note: mistakenly says the letters are put in a wrong, jumbled order
ultimately points to the final letter of the word got

explanation.surface: Given free rein by mistake, someone ended up meddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes T from 'got'; 'mistakenly' rearranges T with FREEREIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere is to involve oneself unasked in other people's affairs, which is meddling.

clue.text: Doctor, I have ambition!

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A patient tells the doctor about their ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is determination and ambition, the motivation to achieve something.

clue.text: Promote development of New Forest

indicators.note: new says the letters of the word Forest are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A call to encourage growth in the New Forest, a national park in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like part of the place name New Forest, a national park in Hampshire, England; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster something is to encourage its growth or promote its development.

clue.text: Passionate type of romantic relationship is doomed, initially

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each of the six words before it

explanation.surface: A passionate kind of romance is doomed from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrid love affair is one full of intense, passionate feeling.

clue.text: Seaman gets new beginning — he's working in menswear

indicators.note: gets new beginning says the seaman's first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a sailor is a seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor takes up a new start in life, working in a menswear shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets new beginning' swaps the S of SAILOR for a T; the replacement letter is not clued, only that the start changes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor makes and alters clothes, traditionally men's suits, so he works in menswear.

clue.text: Genuine regret, after time

indicators.note: after puts the regret piece behind the time piece

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Sincere remorse that comes after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: True and genuine are synonyms: real, not false.

clue.text: Signs figure in harbour towns

indicators.note: in says the figure sits inside the harbour towns

parts.note: ports are towns with harbours
ten is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: Signs showing a number in harbour towns, like dock markers.
explanation.definitionFit: Portents are omens, signs of something coming.

clue.text: Point about playground garden — an example to be followed

indicators.note: about says the point goes around the other pieces

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a playground
Eden is the biblical garden

explanation.surface: A point raised about a playground garden, held up as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec (recreation ground) is a British term for a public playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: A precedent is an earlier case taken as a guide for later ones.

clue.text: Unfortunately goes to butt of jokes

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so goes and to fall into a different order

explanation.surface: Sadly someone always ends up as the target of the jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooge is a performer, or anyone, made the target of others' ridicule.

clue.text: Ultimate in smart town headgear

indicators.note: ultimate in points to the final letter of the word smart

parts.note: urban means relating to a town or city

explanation.surface: The last word in stylish city hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a head covering of cloth wound round the head.

clue.text: An accompanying person in Paris is stifling exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: stifling says the French word wraps around and muffles the exclamation

parts.note: est is French for is
cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A companion in Paris holding back a gasp of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' is a British slang exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is someone who goes along with another as a companion or guard.

clue.text: Entertainment seen in ancient era, bacchanalian, recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
seen in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A show watched in some ancient, wildly drunken age, called back to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Entertainment seen' as the definition; 'seen in' is the hiding signal, so the definition is 'Entertainment' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is a type of nightclub entertainment with song, dance and comedy.

clue.text: First appearance of rime, peer curiously

indicators.note: curiously suggests something odd, so rime and peer appear in a strange order

explanation.surface: A frost's first showing, as someone peers at it with curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the first public performance or showing of a work.

clue.text: Communicators on the rise aim to captivate English Duke

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold, so the reversed word takes the other letters inside
in a down clue, on the rise means the word aim is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Up-and-coming communicators aim to charm an English duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' turns AIM into MIA; 'to captivate' puts ED inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The media are the channels of mass communication, such as press and broadcasting.

clue.text: Jibing at heart when showing prejudice

indicators.note: at heart points to the central letters of the word Jibing

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Taunting at its core reveals prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is an unfair inclination for or against someone, which is prejudice.

clue.text: Assistant interrupted by second digression

indicators.note: interrupted by says the second breaks into the middle of the assistant

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: An assistant is briefly cut off, leading to a digression.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark that departs from the main topic, a digression.

clue.text: Name that's seen on door?

definitions.meaning: informal for a person's name or nickname
the knob or lever used to open a door

explanation.surface: A name you'd see on a door, like a nameplate.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name and also the grip fitted to a door.

clue.text: Good score for child's term for flier

definitions.meaning: one under par on a golf hole
a childish word for a bird

explanation.surface: A child gets a good mark for the word they use for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdie is golf's term for one stroke under par and nursery language for a small bird.

clue.text: Abridge on regular basis — that's important

indicators.note: on regular basis picks every other letter of the word Abridge

explanation.surface: Shortening things routinely is a big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on regular basis' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'Abridge'.
explanation.definitionFit: Big can mean significant or important, as in a big decision.

clue.text: Great hotel for swimming on the whole

indicators.note: swimming suggests things moving about, so the letters of great and hotel float into new places

explanation.surface: A superb hotel for swimming, all things considered.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether can mean all things considered, in general, the overall sense of 'on the whole'.
